newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures close lower on currency/tender.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures close lower on currency/tender.

text.p: UK grain futures closed sharply lower on Thursday under continuing pressure from a strong pound sterling.
The weekly European Union (EU) tender was another factor, but the result was within market expecations.
The EU granted 198,900 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at 18 Ecus rebate and 95,500 tonnes free-market barley at 31.50 Ecus rebate.
"The result is not viewed as bullish, but having said that it was about what we expected," said a trader.
Wheat closed 1.60 to 0.80 stg down after trading 643 lots while barley was 1.35 to 0.50 stg down on 47 lots.
Amsterdam milling futures closed unchanged after trading four lots in December 1996.
UK cash market traders reported only one trade on the fob market when Feb feed wheat fetched 98 stg a tonne ex-east coast ports.
Delivered market traders said there were a number of trades but no tonnage behind any of the business.
